```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
options(width = 120)
```

# Purpose and principles

Each anatomical region is coded as a Yes/No severity variable from its regional
AIS (0-6). The cutoff used so far was AIS >= 3; AIS >= 4 appeared to give a better
model. This document tests that formally and builds the empirical justification
for the choice of the cutoff following three rules:

1. **The cutoff is chosen with the training sample only (2020-2023).** The
   validation sample (2024-2025) is never used to pick the cutoff. It is
   reported afterwards, as a sensitivity analysis, to show that the choice
   generalises.
2. **The criteria are fixed in advance**: AIC and BIC in the training sample and
   repeated, stratified 10-fold cross-validation (AUC, Brier score and log-loss)
   inside the training sample.
3. **Everything is reported**, including the alternative cutoff (>= 3) and a
   cutoff-free alternative (ordinal categories).

The clinical argument (AIS 3 = "serious", AIS 4 = "severe", and AIS 3 is a very
heterogeneous category) is argued in the text of the manuscript; this document
covers the empirical evidence:

* Section 2: 30-day mortality by AIS level in each region (training sample).
* Section 3: comparison of cutoffs with pre-specified criteria (training sample).
* Section 4: sensitivity analysis and transparency (>= 3 vs >= 4).
* Section 5: cutoff-free alternative with ordinal categories.
* Section 6: summary table and suggested wording.

# 1. Data

The cohort is built with the preprocessing code of
`ultimate_validation_preprocessing.Rmd` (all code before the heading
"Preprocessed cohort" is executed). No data file is read or written other than
the raw registry export used by that document.

```{r load-cohort}
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)

preprocessing_path <- file.path(
  "..", "ultimate_validation", "ultimate_validation_preprocessing.Rmd"
)
if (!file.exists(preprocessing_path)) {
  stop("Preprocessing document not found: ", preprocessing_path)
}
preprocessing_lines <- readLines(preprocessing_path, warn = FALSE)
cohort_end_line <- grep("^# Preprocessed cohort", preprocessing_lines)[1]
if (is.na(cohort_end_line)) {
  stop("The heading '# Preprocessed cohort' was not found.")
}

preprocessing_code_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".R")
invisible(knitr::purl(
  text = preprocessing_lines[seq_len(cohort_end_line - 1L)],
  output = preprocessing_code_file,
  documentation = 0L,
  quiet = TRUE
))

preprocessing_env <- new.env(parent = globalenv())
# The preprocessing code opens a table in RStudio; it is not needed here.
preprocessing_env$View <- function(...) invisible(NULL)
invisible(capture.output(
  suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(
    source(preprocessing_code_file, local = preprocessing_env, echo = FALSE)
  ))
))
retrascore_cohort <- preprocessing_env$retrascore_cohort
if (is.null(retrascore_cohort)) {
  stop("The preprocessing code did not create 'retrascore_cohort'.")
}
```

```{r setup-data}
required_packages <- c("pROC", "MASS")
missing_packages <- required_packages[
  !vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
]
if (length(missing_packages) > 0L) {
  stop("Install the following packages: ", paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", "))
}

outcome_variable <- "mortality_30d"
training_years <- 2020:2023
validation_years <- 2024:2025

# The same 11 non-anatomical candidates and 6 anatomical regions used in the
# variable-selection analysis.
non_anatomical <- c(
  "age_category",
  "preinjury_antithrombotic",
  "prehospital_intubation",
  "high_risk_mechanism",
  "pupils",
  "gcs_le_8",
  "hemodynamic_failure",
  "respiratory_failure",
  "coagulopathy_24h",
  "mechanical_ventilation",
  "massive_hemorrhage"
)

regions_df <- data.frame(
  key = c(
    "head", "upper_extremity", "thorax", "abdomen", "lower_extremity", "external"
  ),
  label = c(
    "Head", "Upper extremity", "Thorax", "Abdomen",
    "Lower extremity (incl. pelvis)", "External"
  ),
  ais_var = c(
    "head_ais", "upper_extremity_ais", "thorax_ais", "abdomen_ais",
    "lower_extremity_incl_pelvis_ais", "external_ais"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

needed_variables <- c(
  "row_id", "trauma_year", outcome_variable, non_anatomical, regions_df$ais_var
)
if (!all(needed_variables %in% names(retrascore_cohort))) {
  stop(
    "Missing variables: ",
    paste(setdiff(needed_variables, names(retrascore_cohort)), collapse = ", ")
  )
}

# Derived severity variables for every region:
#   <key>_ge2 ... <key>_ge5 : Yes if regional AIS >= 2 ... >= 5, otherwise No
#   <key>_ord               : ordinal categories 0 / 1-2 / 3 / 4-6
add_derived_columns <- function(data) {
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(regions_df))) {
    ais <- data[[regions_df$ais_var[i]]]
    for (cutoff in 2:5) {
      data[[paste0(regions_df$key[i], "_ge", cutoff)]] <- factor(
        ifelse(ais >= cutoff, "Yes", "No"),
        levels = c("No", "Yes")
      )
    }
    data[[paste0(regions_df$key[i], "_ord")]] <- factor(
      case_when(
        ais == 0 ~ "0",
        ais <= 2 ~ "1-2",
        ais == 3 ~ "3",
        ais >= 4 ~ "4-6"
      ),
      levels = c("0", "1-2", "3", "4-6")
    )
  }
  data
}

# Complete cases for the outcome and all candidate predictors (same patients as
# in the variable-selection analysis).
cutoff_data <- retrascore_cohort[
  complete.cases(retrascore_cohort[, needed_variables, drop = FALSE]),
  needed_variables,
  drop = FALSE
]
cutoff_data <- add_derived_columns(droplevels(cutoff_data))

training_data <- cutoff_data[cutoff_data$trauma_year %in% training_years, , drop = FALSE]
validation_data <- cutoff_data[cutoff_data$trauma_year %in% validation_years, , drop = FALSE]
if (nrow(training_data) == 0L || nrow(validation_data) == 0L) {
  stop("The training or validation sample is empty.")
}

knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Sample = c("Training (2020-2023)", "Validation (2024-2025)"),
    Patients = c(nrow(training_data), nrow(validation_data)),
    `Deaths within 30 days` = c(
      sum(training_data[[outcome_variable]]),
      sum(validation_data[[outcome_variable]])
    ),
    `Mortality (%)` = round(100 * c(
      mean(training_data[[outcome_variable]]),
      mean(validation_data[[outcome_variable]])
    ), 1),
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  align = c("l", "r", "r", "r"),
  caption = "Analysis samples (complete cases)"
)

fmt_p <- function(p) format.pval(p, digits = 3, eps = 0.001)
```

# 2. 30-day mortality by AIS level in each region (training sample)

If the cutoff is empirically justified, the 30-day mortality should rise
clearly between the categories that the cutoff separates. The table shows, for
each region, deaths / patients (mortality) at each AIS level, using only the
2020-2023 training sample. The figure shows the same with 95% Wilson confidence
intervals (levels with fewer than 10 patients are not drawn); dotted lines mark
the two candidate cutoffs (between 2 and 3 for >= 3, between 3 and 4 for >= 4).

```{r mortality-by-level}
mortality_by_level <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(regions_df)), function(i) {
  ais <- training_data[[regions_df$ais_var[i]]]
  y <- training_data[[outcome_variable]]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(0:6, function(level) {
    in_level <- ais == level
    n <- sum(in_level)
    d <- sum(y[in_level])
    ci <- if (n > 0L) {
      suppressWarnings(prop.test(d, n, correct = FALSE)$conf.int)
    } else {
      c(NA_real_, NA_real_)
    }
    data.frame(
      Region = regions_df$label[i],
      AIS = level,
      N = n,
      Deaths = d,
      Mortality = if (n > 0L) 100 * d / n else NA_real_,
      Lower = 100 * ci[1],
      Upper = 100 * ci[2],
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }))
}))

mortality_wide <- sapply(regions_df$label, function(region_label) {
  rows <- mortality_by_level[mortality_by_level$Region == region_label, ]
  ifelse(
    rows$N == 0L,
    "-",
    sprintf("%d/%d (%.1f%%)", rows$Deaths, rows$N, rows$Mortality)
  )
})
mortality_wide <- data.frame(`Regional AIS` = 0:6, mortality_wide, check.names = FALSE)

knitr::kable(
  mortality_wide,
  align = c("c", rep("r", nrow(regions_df))),
  caption = "30-day deaths / patients (mortality) by regional AIS level, training sample 2020-2023"
)
```

```{r mortality-plot, fig.width=11, fig.height=6.5, fig.cap="30-day mortality by regional AIS level (training sample). Dotted lines: candidate cutoffs >= 3 (between 2 and 3) and >= 4 (between 3 and 4)."}
old_par <- par(mfrow = c(2, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
for (region_label in regions_df$label) {
  rows <- mortality_by_level[
    mortality_by_level$Region == region_label & mortality_by_level$N >= 10L, ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]
  if (nrow(rows) == 0L) {
    next
  }
  plot(
    rows$AIS, rows$Mortality,
    type = "b", pch = 19,
    xlim = c(0, 6), ylim = c(0, max(rows$Upper, na.rm = TRUE)),
    xlab = "Regional AIS", ylab = "30-day mortality (%)",
    main = region_label
  )
  segments(rows$AIS, rows$Lower, rows$AIS, rows$Upper)
  abline(v = c(2.5, 3.5), lty = 3, col = "grey50")
}
par(old_par)
```

The two contrasts that decide the cutoff are shown next, using only patients
injured in the region:

* **AIS 3 vs AIS 1-2**: if AIS 3 behaves like minor injuries, it should not be
  called "severe" (supports a cutoff of >= 4).
* **AIS 4-6 vs AIS 3**: if mortality jumps between 3 and 4, the two levels
  should not be pooled (supports separating them at >= 4).

The comparisons are crude (unadjusted); adjusted estimates are in Section 5.

```{r mortality-contrasts}
compare_groups <- function(data, ais_var, hi_levels, lo_levels) {
  y <- data[[outcome_variable]]
  ais <- data[[ais_var]]
  y_hi <- y[ais %in% hi_levels]
  y_lo <- y[ais %in% lo_levels]
  if (length(y_hi) < 5L || length(y_lo) < 5L) {
    return(data.frame(
      `N (higher)` = length(y_hi), `N (lower)` = length(y_lo),
      `Mortality higher (%)` = NA_real_, `Mortality lower (%)` = NA_real_,
      `Risk difference, pp (95% CI)` = "n/a", `Odds ratio (95% CI)` = "n/a",
      `p (Fisher)` = "n/a", check.names = FALSE
    ))
  }
  rd_test <- suppressWarnings(prop.test(
    c(sum(y_hi), sum(y_lo)), c(length(y_hi), length(y_lo)), correct = FALSE
  ))
  fisher <- fisher.test(matrix(
    c(sum(y_hi), length(y_hi) - sum(y_hi), sum(y_lo), length(y_lo) - sum(y_lo)),
    nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE
  ))
  risk_difference <- 100 * (mean(y_hi) - mean(y_lo))
  data.frame(
    `N (higher)` = length(y_hi),
    `N (lower)` = length(y_lo),
    `Mortality higher (%)` = 100 * mean(y_hi),
    `Mortality lower (%)` = 100 * mean(y_lo),
    `Risk difference, pp (95% CI)` = sprintf(
      "%.1f (%.1f to %.1f)", risk_difference,
      100 * rd_test$conf.int[1], 100 * rd_test$conf.int[2]
    ),
    `Odds ratio (95% CI)` = sprintf(
      "%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", fisher$estimate, fisher$conf.int[1], fisher$conf.int[2]
    ),
    `p (Fisher)` = fmt_p(fisher$p.value),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}

contrast_definitions <- list(
  list(name = "AIS 3 vs AIS 1-2", hi = 3, lo = 1:2),
  list(name = "AIS 4-6 vs AIS 3", hi = 4:6, lo = 3)
)

contrast_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(regions_df)), function(i) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(contrast_definitions, function(contrast) {
    cbind(
      Region = regions_df$label[i],
      Contrast = contrast$name,
      compare_groups(training_data, regions_df$ais_var[i], contrast$hi, contrast$lo),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }))
}))

knitr::kable(
  contrast_table,
  digits = 1,
  align = c("l", "l", rep("r", 7)),
  caption = "Unadjusted 30-day mortality contrasts between adjacent AIS categories (training sample)"
)
```

# 3. Comparison of cutoffs with pre-specified criteria (training sample only)

## 3.1 Models and criteria

For each candidate cutoff the same logistic model is fitted in the 2020-2023
training sample: the 11 non-anatomical candidate predictors plus the six
anatomical regions, **all coded with the same cutoff** (severe = regional AIS >=
cutoff). Using the full 17-predictor model removes the influence of variable
selection on the comparison. Because the models are not nested (they differ in
the coding of the same variables), the likelihood-ratio test is not valid, so
the comparison uses:

* **AIC and BIC** (training sample).
* **Repeated stratified 10-fold cross-validation inside the training sample**
  (10 repeats, folds identical for all models): AUC, Brier score and log-loss
  computed on the pooled out-of-fold predictions of each repeat.

Note that the cutoffs >= 5 (and, in some regions, >= 4) classify very few
patients as severe, notably in the upper extremity and external regions (see the
table below). Estimates for those regions are unstable, so the comparison should
rely mainly on >= 3 versus >= 4.

```{r model-specs}
spec_formulas <- list(
  ge2 = reformulate(c(non_anatomical, paste0(regions_df$key, "_ge2")), response = outcome_variable),
  ge3 = reformulate(c(non_anatomical, paste0(regions_df$key, "_ge3")), response = outcome_variable),
  ge4 = reformulate(c(non_anatomical, paste0(regions_df$key, "_ge4")), response = outcome_variable),
  ge5 = reformulate(c(non_anatomical, paste0(regions_df$key, "_ge5")), response = outcome_variable),
  ordinal = reformulate(c(non_anatomical, paste0(regions_df$key, "_ord")), response = outcome_variable)
)
spec_labels <- c(
  ge2 = "Binary: severe = AIS >= 2",
  ge3 = "Binary: severe = AIS >= 3",
  ge4 = "Binary: severe = AIS >= 4",
  ge5 = "Binary: severe = AIS >= 5",
  ordinal = "Ordinal: 0 / 1-2 / 3 / 4-6"
)

training_fits <- lapply(spec_formulas, function(model_formula) {
  glm(
    formula = model_formula,
    data = training_data,
    family = binomial(link = "logit")
  )
})
if (!all(vapply(training_fits, function(m) isTRUE(m$converged), logical(1)))) {
  stop("At least one logistic model did not converge.")
}

severity_prevalence <- data.frame(
  Region = regions_df$label,
  `Severe if AIS >= 3, n (%)` = vapply(seq_len(nrow(regions_df)), function(i) {
    n <- sum(training_data[[regions_df$ais_var[i]]] >= 3)
    sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", n, 100 * n / nrow(training_data))
  }, character(1)),
  `Severe if AIS >= 4, n (%)` = vapply(seq_len(nrow(regions_df)), function(i) {
    n <- sum(training_data[[regions_df$ais_var[i]]] >= 4)
    sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", n, 100 * n / nrow(training_data))
  }, character(1)),
  check.names = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(
  severity_prevalence,
  align = c("l", "r", "r"),
  caption = "Patients classified as severe in each region under the two main cutoffs (training sample)"
)
```

```{r cross-validation}
cv_folds <- 10L
cv_repeats <- 10L
cv_seed <- 20261109L

fast_auc <- function(predicted, observed) {
  n_events <- sum(observed == 1)
  n_non_events <- sum(observed == 0)
  (sum(rank(predicted)[observed == 1]) - n_events * (n_events + 1) / 2) /
    (n_events * n_non_events)
}

stratified_folds <- function(y, k, seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  fold_id <- integer(length(y))
  for (class_value in unique(y)) {
    idx <- which(y == class_value)
    fold_id[idx] <- sample(rep_len(seq_len(k), length(idx)))
  }
  fold_id
}

# Very sparse categories (for example AIS >= 5 in the upper extremity, with a
# single patient in the training sample) can be absent from a training fold. A
# predictor with a single value in the fold cannot be estimated, so it is left
# out of that fold's model.
drop_constant_terms <- function(model_formula, data) {
  term_labels <- attr(terms(model_formula), "term.labels")
  has_variation <- vapply(term_labels, function(term_label) {
    values <- data[[term_label]]
    length(unique(values[!is.na(values)])) >= 2L
  }, logical(1))
  reformulate(term_labels[has_variation], response = outcome_variable)
}

# Out-of-fold predicted probabilities: one column per repeat. The folds depend
# only on the outcome and the seed, so they are identical for every model.
cv_oof_predictions <- function(model_formula, data, k, repeats, seed) {
  y <- data[[outcome_variable]]
  oof <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(data), ncol = repeats)
  for (r in seq_len(repeats)) {
    fold_id <- stratified_folds(y, k, seed + r)
    for (f in seq_len(k)) {
      in_training_fold <- fold_id != f
      fold_training_data <- data[in_training_fold, , drop = FALSE]
      fit <- suppressWarnings(glm(
        formula = drop_constant_terms(model_formula, fold_training_data),
        data = fold_training_data,
        family = binomial(link = "logit")
      ))
      oof[!in_training_fold, r] <- suppressWarnings(predict(
        fit, newdata = data[!in_training_fold, , drop = FALSE], type = "response"
      ))
    }
  }
  oof
}

oof_metrics <- function(oof, y) {
  clip <- function(p) pmin(pmax(p, 1e-12), 1 - 1e-12)
  data.frame(
    repeat_id = seq_len(ncol(oof)),
    AUC = apply(oof, 2, fast_auc, observed = y),
    Brier = apply(oof, 2, function(p) mean((y - p)^2)),
    LogLoss = apply(oof, 2, function(p) -mean(y * log(clip(p)) + (1 - y) * log(1 - clip(p))))
  )
}

# All specifications are cross-validated here (the ordinal one is used in
# Section 5).
cv_oof <- lapply(spec_formulas, cv_oof_predictions,
  data = training_data, k = cv_folds, repeats = cv_repeats, seed = cv_seed
)
cv_metrics <- lapply(cv_oof, oof_metrics, y = training_data[[outcome_variable]])

cv_numeric <- data.frame(
  Model = unname(spec_labels[names(spec_formulas)]),
  Parameters = vapply(training_fits, function(m) sum(!is.na(coef(m))), numeric(1)),
  AIC = vapply(training_fits, AIC, numeric(1)),
  BIC = vapply(training_fits, BIC, numeric(1)),
  CV_AUC = vapply(cv_metrics, function(m) mean(m$AUC), numeric(1)),
  CV_AUC_SD = vapply(cv_metrics, function(m) sd(m$AUC), numeric(1)),
  CV_Brier = vapply(cv_metrics, function(m) mean(m$Brier), numeric(1)),
  CV_LogLoss = vapply(cv_metrics, function(m) mean(m$LogLoss), numeric(1)),
  row.names = names(spec_formulas),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

format_cv_table <- function(spec_keys) {
  rows <- cv_numeric[spec_keys, , drop = FALSE]
  data.frame(
    Model = rows$Model,
    Parameters = rows$Parameters,
    AIC = round(rows$AIC, 1),
    BIC = round(rows$BIC, 1),
    `CV AUC (mean)` = round(rows$CV_AUC, 4),
    `CV AUC (SD over repeats)` = round(rows$CV_AUC_SD, 4),
    `CV Brier` = round(rows$CV_Brier, 4),
    `CV log-loss` = round(rows$CV_LogLoss, 4),
    check.names = FALSE,
    row.names = NULL
  )
}
```

## 3.2 Global cutoff (all regions coded with the same cutoff)

Lower AIC / BIC, higher CV AUC and lower CV Brier / log-loss are better. The SD
of the CV AUC only reflects the randomness of the fold assignment, not
sampling uncertainty.

```{r cutoff-table}
knitr::kable(
  format_cv_table(c("ge2", "ge3", "ge4", "ge5")),
  align = c("l", rep("r", 7)),
  caption = "Comparison of global cutoffs in the training sample (2020-2023): information criteria and cross-validated performance"
)
```

The primary comparison is >= 4 against >= 3. Positive differences favour the
cutoff >= 4. The paired DeLong test uses the pooled out-of-fold predictions of
the first cross-validation repeat (same patients in both models); it is
indicative, since out-of-fold predictions are not fully independent.

```{r cutoff-paired}
y_training <- training_data[[outcome_variable]]

paired_delong <- function(y, p_new, p_ref) {
  roc_new <- pROC::roc(y, p_new, levels = c(0, 1), direction = "<", quiet = TRUE)
  roc_ref <- pROC::roc(y, p_ref, levels = c(0, 1), direction = "<", quiet = TRUE)
  test <- pROC::roc.test(roc_new, roc_ref, method = "delong", paired = TRUE)
  difference <- as.numeric(pROC::auc(roc_new)) - as.numeric(pROC::auc(roc_ref))
  z <- abs(as.numeric(test$statistic))
  se <- if (is.finite(z) && z > 0) abs(difference) / z else NA_real_
  data.frame(
    difference = difference,
    lower = difference - 1.96 * se,
    upper = difference + 1.96 * se,
    p = test$p.value
  )
}

delong_ge4_vs_ge3 <- paired_delong(y_training, cv_oof$ge4[, 1], cv_oof$ge3[, 1])
auc_difference_by_repeat <- cv_metrics$ge4$AUC - cv_metrics$ge3$AUC

primary_comparison <- data.frame(
  Criterion = c(
    "AIC (AIC of >= 3 minus AIC of >= 4)",
    "BIC (BIC of >= 3 minus BIC of >= 4)",
    "CV AUC (>= 4 minus >= 3), mean over repeats [range]",
    "CV log-loss (>= 3 minus >= 4), mean over repeats",
    "CV Brier score (>= 3 minus >= 4), mean over repeats",
    "Paired DeLong, first repeat: AUC difference (95% CI), p"
  ),
  `Favours >= 4 if` = c(
    "positive", "positive", "positive", "positive", "positive", "positive"
  ),
  Value = c(
    sprintf("%.1f", cv_numeric["ge3", "AIC"] - cv_numeric["ge4", "AIC"]),
    sprintf("%.1f", cv_numeric["ge3", "BIC"] - cv_numeric["ge4", "BIC"]),
    sprintf(
      "%.4f [%.4f to %.4f]", mean(auc_difference_by_repeat),
      min(auc_difference_by_repeat), max(auc_difference_by_repeat)
    ),
    sprintf("%.4f", cv_numeric["ge3", "CV_LogLoss"] - cv_numeric["ge4", "CV_LogLoss"]),
    sprintf("%.4f", cv_numeric["ge3", "CV_Brier"] - cv_numeric["ge4", "CV_Brier"]),
    sprintf(
      "%.4f (%.4f to %.4f), p = %s", delong_ge4_vs_ge3$difference,
      delong_ge4_vs_ge3$lower, delong_ge4_vs_ge3$upper, fmt_p(delong_ge4_vs_ge3$p)
    )
  ),
  check.names = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(
  primary_comparison,
  align = c("l", "c", "r"),
  caption = "Primary comparison: severe = AIS >= 4 versus AIS >= 3 (training sample only)"
)
```

Rule of thumb for AIC / BIC: a difference > 10 is strong evidence for the model
with the lower value, 4-7 clearly favours it, and < 2 means that the models are
practically equivalent.

## 3.3 Is the best cutoff the same in every region?

Each region is recoded in turn with cutoffs >= 2 to >= 5, keeping the other five
regions at >= 4. The table shows the AIC increase over the best cutoff of that
region (0 = best). If all regions prefer the same cutoff, a single global cutoff
is easy to defend; if one region prefers a different one, this should be
discussed (region-specific cutoffs are possible but add complexity).

```{r region-scan}
region_scan <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(regions_df)), function(i) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(2:5, function(cutoff) {
    region_terms <- paste0(regions_df$key, "_ge4")
    region_terms[i] <- paste0(regions_df$key[i], "_ge", cutoff)
    fit <- glm(
      formula = reformulate(c(non_anatomical, region_terms), response = outcome_variable),
      data = training_data,
      family = binomial(link = "logit")
    )
    data.frame(
      Region = regions_df$label[i],
      Cutoff = paste0(">= ", cutoff),
      AIC = AIC(fit),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }))
}))
region_scan$Delta <- ave(region_scan$AIC, region_scan$Region, FUN = function(x) x - min(x))

region_scan_wide <- tapply(
  region_scan$Delta, list(region_scan$Region, region_scan$Cutoff), sum
)
region_scan_wide <- region_scan_wide[regions_df$label, , drop = FALSE]
region_scan_table <- data.frame(
  Region = rownames(region_scan_wide),
  round(region_scan_wide, 1),
  `Best cutoff` = colnames(region_scan_wide)[apply(region_scan_wide, 1, which.min)],
  check.names = FALSE,
  row.names = NULL
)

knitr::kable(
  region_scan_table,
  align = c("l", rep("r", ncol(region_scan_wide)), "c"),
  caption = "Increase in AIC over the best cutoff of each region (other regions fixed at >= 4), training sample"
)
```

# 4. Sensitivity analysis and transparency: >= 3 versus >= 4

The cutoff has been chosen in Section 3 without using the validation sample.
Here both cutoffs are fully reported, and the 2024-2025 validation sample is
used **only to check that the conclusion generalises**, not to choose.

## 4.1 Performance in training and validation samples

Models fitted in the training sample (2020-2023) and evaluated in both samples.
The DeLong test compares the two AUCs on the same patients (paired).

```{r validation-performance}
evaluate_model <- function(model, data, sample_label, spec_key) {
  y <- data[[outcome_variable]]
  p <- predict(model, newdata = data, type = "response")
  roc_object <- pROC::roc(y, p, levels = c(0, 1), direction = "<", quiet = TRUE)
  auc_ci <- as.numeric(pROC::ci.auc(roc_object, method = "delong"))
  data.frame(
    Spec = spec_key,
    Model = unname(spec_labels[spec_key]),
    Sample = sample_label,
    N = length(y),
    Deaths = sum(y),
    AUC = auc_ci[2],
    `AUC 95% CI` = sprintf("%.3f-%.3f", auc_ci[1], auc_ci[3]),
    Brier = mean((y - p)^2),
    check.names = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

performance_specs <- c("ge3", "ge4", "ordinal")
validation_performance <- do.call(rbind, lapply(performance_specs, function(spec_key) {
  rbind(
    evaluate_model(training_fits[[spec_key]], training_data, "Training (2020-2023)", spec_key),
    evaluate_model(training_fits[[spec_key]], validation_data, "Validation (2024-2025)", spec_key)
  )
}))

knitr::kable(
  validation_performance[
    validation_performance$Spec %in% c("ge3", "ge4"),
    c("Model", "Sample", "N", "Deaths", "AUC", "AUC 95% CI", "Brier")
  ],
  digits = 3,
  row.names = FALSE,
  align = c("l", "l", rep("r", 5)),
  caption = "Performance of the logistic models with the cutoff >= 3 and >= 4 (full 17-predictor models)"
)

validation_delong <- paired_delong(
  validation_data[[outcome_variable]],
  predict(training_fits$ge4, newdata = validation_data, type = "response"),
  predict(training_fits$ge3, newdata = validation_data, type = "response")
)
```

Validation AUC, cutoff >= 4 minus cutoff >= 3: **`r sprintf("%.4f (95%% CI %.4f to %.4f), paired DeLong p = %s", validation_delong$difference, validation_delong$lower, validation_delong$upper, fmt_p(validation_delong$p))`**.

## 4.2 Does the cutoff change which variables are selected?

Bidirectional stepwise AIC selection (same procedure as in the main analysis)
starting from the full model of each cutoff, in the training sample.

```{r stepwise-by-cutoff}
step_models <- list()
for (cutoff_key in c("ge3", "ge4")) {
  full_model_for_step <- glm(
    formula = spec_formulas[[cutoff_key]],
    data = training_data,
    family = binomial(link = "logit"),
    na.action = na.fail
  )
  step_models[[cutoff_key]] <- MASS::stepAIC(
    full_model_for_step, direction = "both", trace = FALSE
  )
}

variable_of_term <- function(term) sub("_(ge[0-9]|ord)$", "", term)
selected_variables <- lapply(step_models, function(model) {
  variable_of_term(attr(terms(model), "term.labels"))
})
all_variables <- c(non_anatomical, regions_df$key)
predictor_names <- ifelse(
  all_variables %in% regions_df$key,
  paste0(regions_df$label[match(all_variables, regions_df$key)], " (regional severity)"),
  all_variables
)

stepwise_selection_table <- data.frame(
  Predictor = predictor_names,
  `Cutoff >= 3` = ifelse(all_variables %in% selected_variables$ge3, "selected", "-"),
  `Cutoff >= 4` = ifelse(all_variables %in% selected_variables$ge4, "selected", "-"),
  check.names = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(
  stepwise_selection_table,
  align = c("l", "c", "c"),
  caption = "Predictors retained by stepwise AIC under each cutoff (training sample)"
)

stepwise_performance <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("ge3", "ge4"), function(spec_key) {
  rbind(
    evaluate_model(step_models[[spec_key]], training_data, "Training (2020-2023)", spec_key),
    evaluate_model(step_models[[spec_key]], validation_data, "Validation (2024-2025)", spec_key)
  )
}))
stepwise_performance$Model <- paste(
  "Stepwise-AIC model,", sub("Binary: severe = ", "severe = ", stepwise_performance$Model)
)
stepwise_performance$Predictors <- rep(
  vapply(step_models, function(m) length(attr(terms(m), "term.labels")), numeric(1)),
  each = 2
)

knitr::kable(
  stepwise_performance[, c("Model", "Predictors", "Sample", "AUC", "AUC 95% CI", "Brier")],
  digits = 3,
  row.names = FALSE,
  align = c("l", "r", "l", "r", "r", "r"),
  caption = "Performance of the stepwise-AIC models under each cutoff"
)

stepwise_validation_delong <- paired_delong(
  validation_data[[outcome_variable]],
  predict(step_models$ge4, newdata = validation_data, type = "response"),
  predict(step_models$ge3, newdata = validation_data, type = "response")
)
```

Validation AUC of the stepwise model, cutoff >= 4 minus cutoff >= 3: **`r sprintf("%.4f (95%% CI %.4f to %.4f), paired DeLong p = %s", stepwise_validation_delong$difference, stepwise_validation_delong$lower, stepwise_validation_delong$upper, fmt_p(stepwise_validation_delong$p))`**.

## 4.3 Are the other effects stable?

Odds ratios (Wald 95% CI) of the full models with both cutoffs. The
non-anatomical predictors should keep similar estimates; the region rows have a
different meaning in each column (severe = AIS >= 3 vs AIS >= 4).

```{r odds-ratio-stability}
odds_ratio_table <- function(model) {
  coefficients_matrix <- summary(model)$coefficients
  est <- coefficients_matrix[, "Estimate"]
  se <- coefficients_matrix[, "Std. Error"]
  data.frame(
    term = rownames(coefficients_matrix),
    normalised = sub("_ge[0-9]Yes$", "_severe", rownames(coefficients_matrix)),
    or = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", exp(est), exp(est - 1.96 * se), exp(est + 1.96 * se)),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}
or_ge3 <- odds_ratio_table(training_fits$ge3)
or_ge4 <- odds_ratio_table(training_fits$ge4)
or_ge3 <- or_ge3[or_ge3$term != "(Intercept)", ]

or_comparison <- data.frame(
  Term = or_ge3$term,
  `OR, severe = AIS >= 3` = or_ge3$or,
  `OR, severe = AIS >= 4` = or_ge4$or[match(or_ge3$normalised, or_ge4$normalised)],
  check.names = FALSE,
  row.names = NULL
)
or_comparison$Term <- sub("_ge3Yes$", " (severe)", or_comparison$Term)

knitr::kable(
  or_comparison,
  align = c("l", "r", "r"),
  caption = "Odds ratios of the full logistic models (training sample)"
)
```

# 5. Cutoff-free alternative: ordinal categories

To avoid depending on a single threshold, each region is also coded with four
categories: **0** (no injury in the region), **1-2** (minor/moderate), **3**
(serious) and **4-6** (severe or worse). The model estimates a separate effect
for each category, so the data decide whether AIS 3 behaves like the lower or
like the higher categories. The ordinal model uses more parameters (3 per
region instead of 1), which AIC/BIC and cross-validation penalise.

## 5.1 Binary cutoffs versus ordinal coding

```{r ordinal-comparison}
knitr::kable(
  format_cv_table(c("ge3", "ge4", "ordinal")),
  align = c("l", rep("r", 7)),
  caption = "Binary cutoffs versus ordinal coding in the training sample (information criteria and cross-validation)"
)

ordinal_vs_ge4 <- paired_delong(y_training, cv_oof$ordinal[, 1], cv_oof$ge4[, 1])
```

Out-of-fold AUC of the ordinal model minus that of the cutoff >= 4 model (first
repeat, paired DeLong): **`r sprintf("%.4f (95%% CI %.4f to %.4f), p = %s", ordinal_vs_ge4$difference, ordinal_vs_ge4$lower, ordinal_vs_ge4$upper, fmt_p(ordinal_vs_ge4$p))`**.
If the ordinal model does not outperform the binary model with cutoff >= 4 on
AIC/BIC and cross-validation, the simpler binary coding is justified.

```{r ordinal-validation}
knitr::kable(
  validation_performance[
    , c("Model", "Sample", "N", "Deaths", "AUC", "AUC 95% CI", "Brier")
  ],
  digits = 3,
  row.names = FALSE,
  align = c("l", "l", rep("r", 5)),
  caption = "Training and validation performance (validation shown only as a check; it was not used to choose the coding)"
)
```

## 5.2 Adjusted effect of each category

Adjusted odds ratios from the ordinal model (reference: AIS 0 in that region,
adjusted for all other predictors). The last two columns test directly whether
AIS 4-6 differs from AIS 3 in the same region. A significant difference with
OR(4-6 vs 3) clearly above 1 means that levels 3 and 4-6 should not be pooled
under the same "severe" label; an OR(3 vs 0) close to 1 for AIS 3 would show
that AIS 3 carries little additional risk on its own.

```{r ordinal-effects}
ordinal_fit <- training_fits$ordinal
ordinal_coefficients <- summary(ordinal_fit)$coefficients
ordinal_vcov <- vcov(ordinal_fit)

format_or <- function(estimate, std_error) {
  sprintf(
    "%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", exp(estimate),
    exp(estimate - 1.96 * std_error), exp(estimate + 1.96 * std_error)
  )
}

ordinal_effects <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(regions_df)), function(i) {
  key <- regions_df$key[i]
  names_needed <- paste0(key, c("_ord1-2", "_ord3", "_ord4-6"))
  if (!all(names_needed %in% rownames(ordinal_coefficients))) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  b <- ordinal_coefficients[names_needed, "Estimate"]
  s <- ordinal_coefficients[names_needed, "Std. Error"]
  difference <- b[3] - b[2]
  difference_se <- sqrt(
    ordinal_vcov[names_needed[3], names_needed[3]] +
      ordinal_vcov[names_needed[2], names_needed[2]] -
      2 * ordinal_vcov[names_needed[3], names_needed[2]]
  )
  data.frame(
    Region = regions_df$label[i],
    `OR AIS 1-2 vs 0` = format_or(b[1], s[1]),
    `OR AIS 3 vs 0` = format_or(b[2], s[2]),
    `OR AIS 4-6 vs 0` = format_or(b[3], s[3]),
    `OR AIS 4-6 vs 3` = format_or(difference, difference_se),
    `p (4-6 vs 3)` = fmt_p(2 * pnorm(-abs(difference / difference_se))),
    check.names = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}))

knitr::kable(
  ordinal_effects,
  align = c("l", rep("r", 5)),
  row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Adjusted odds ratios by AIS category (ordinal model, training sample)"
)
```

# 6. Summary and suggested wording

```{r summary-table}
validation_auc <- function(spec_key) {
  validation_performance$AUC[
    validation_performance$Spec == spec_key &
      validation_performance$Sample == "Validation (2024-2025)"
  ]
}

summary_table <- data.frame(
  Criterion = c(
    "AIC (training)", "BIC (training)", "CV AUC (training)",
    "CV Brier score (training)", "CV log-loss (training)",
    "Validation AUC (check only, 2024-2025)"
  ),
  `Severe = AIS >= 3` = c(
    sprintf("%.1f", cv_numeric["ge3", "AIC"]),
    sprintf("%.1f", cv_numeric["ge3", "BIC"]),
    sprintf("%.4f", cv_numeric["ge3", "CV_AUC"]),
    sprintf("%.4f", cv_numeric["ge3", "CV_Brier"]),
    sprintf("%.4f", cv_numeric["ge3", "CV_LogLoss"]),
    sprintf("%.4f", validation_auc("ge3"))
  ),
  `Severe = AIS >= 4` = c(
    sprintf("%.1f", cv_numeric["ge4", "AIC"]),
    sprintf("%.1f", cv_numeric["ge4", "BIC"]),
    sprintf("%.4f", cv_numeric["ge4", "CV_AUC"]),
    sprintf("%.4f", cv_numeric["ge4", "CV_Brier"]),
    sprintf("%.4f", cv_numeric["ge4", "CV_LogLoss"]),
    sprintf("%.4f", validation_auc("ge4"))
  ),
  `Ordinal (0 / 1-2 / 3 / 4-6)` = c(
    sprintf("%.1f", cv_numeric["ordinal", "AIC"]),
    sprintf("%.1f", cv_numeric["ordinal", "BIC"]),
    sprintf("%.4f", cv_numeric["ordinal", "CV_AUC"]),
    sprintf("%.4f", cv_numeric["ordinal", "CV_Brier"]),
    sprintf("%.4f", cv_numeric["ordinal", "CV_LogLoss"]),
    sprintf("%.4f", validation_auc("ordinal"))
  ),
  check.names = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(
  summary_table,
  align = c("l", "r", "r", "r"),
  caption = "Summary of the evidence for the choice of the cutoff"
)
```

**Suggested wording** (adapt the bracketed parts to the results above):

*Methods.* "Regional injury severity was defined as AIS >= 4 (severe) versus
AIS <= 3. This cutoff was selected using the training sample (2020-2023) only,
comparing cutoffs of AIS >= 2 to >= 5 with the Akaike and Bayesian information
criteria and 10-fold cross-validation repeated 10 times (AUC, Brier score and
log-loss). The validation sample (2024-2025) was not used to choose the cutoff.
As sensitivity analyses, we repeated the analysis with a cutoff of AIS >= 3 and
with ordinal categories (0, 1-2, 3 and 4-6)."

*Results.* "In the training sample, the cutoff of AIS >= 4 had [lower AIC and
BIC (difference [x] and [y])] and [higher cross-validated AUC ([a] vs [b])] than
AIS >= 3. [30-day mortality increased from [p1]% in AIS 3 to [p2]% in AIS 4-6
for [region(s)], whereas AIS 3 was similar to AIS 1-2 ([p3]%)]. In the
validation sample the AUC was [c] for AIS >= 4 and [d] for AIS >= 3 [(paired
DeLong p = [p])], and the variables selected by stepwise regression were
[the same / similar] with both cutoffs (Supplementary Table [x])."

*Discussion/limitations.* "The cutoff is a modelling choice; ordinal coding,
which does not require a single threshold, gave [similar / not better]
performance at the cost of more parameters. Cross-validation estimates of the
difference between cutoffs are correlated across folds and should be read as
descriptive."
